newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS ROMP TO 10-TRY WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS ROMP TO 10-TRY WIN.

text.p: The British Lions completed the provincial games of their South African tour with a 10-try flourish against Northern Free State on Tuesday.

Right wing Tony Underwood scored a first half hat-trick while fullback Tim Stimpson crossed twice and was successful with eight out of 11 kicks at goal for a personal haul of 27 points as the Lions racked up their highest score of the tour in winning 67-39.

Northern Free State were never really in the match and spent much of the afternoon chasing shadows. But they entered into the spirit of a free-flowing game and were rewarded with four tries of their own.
Underwood completed his hat-trick in 22 minutes with the Lions' first three tries -- all converted by Stimpson who also kicked a penalty in the opening quarter to give the Lions a 24-7 lead.
The wing's best score was his third, straight from the restart after his second, which ended with flanker Neil Back popping up at outside centre to give the scoring pass.
Lock Simon Shaw scored two tries -- one started deep in the Lions 22 and seemingly involving all 15 players at least once before the strapping forward plunged over from five metres.
The dynamic performances of Back on tour were finally rewarded when he scored his first try of the trip. Scrum-half Kyran Bracken and hooker Mark Regan also made the scoresheet.

The Lions produced some compelling passages of play to complete their 11th victory from 12 matches. It was the fourth time they had broken 50 points and they eclipsed their previous highest score of 64 against Mpumalanga.
The home side, one of the weakest provinces, profited from a penalty try in the seventh minute when centre Nick Beal shouldered winger Willie Nagel off the ball in the in-goal area.
They were fortunate to be awarded a second try on the stroke of halftime -- fullback Michael Ehrentraut was shown by television replays not to have grounded the ball beyond the goal-line.
The final match of the tour is on Saturday when the Lions take on South Africa in the thrid test in Johannesburg. They have already won the series 2-0.

Northern Free State: 15-Michael Ehrentraut (John Burrows 68); 14-Trevor Harmse, 13-Albertus van Buuren, 12-Tommie de Beer, 11-Willie Nagel; 10-Eric Herbert, 9-Jurrie Jerling (captain); 8-Martin Venter, 7-Eugene Delport (Andre Fouche 75), 6-Henry Kershaw, 5-Stephen Nieiwenhuyzen, 4-Koos Heydenrich, 3-Baksteen Nell, 2-Otto Wagener, 1-Kobie Applegryn.

British Lions: 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-Tony Stanger, 13-Allan Bateman, 12-Nick Beal, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt 9-Kyran Bracken (Austin Healey 55); 8-Tony Diprose, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-David Young, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Jason Leonard (captain) (Graham Rowntree 41).
